summary:
FMLink reports on US labor market data and healthcare facilities management hiring, framed around jobs listed in its Career Center. Healthcare hiring continued in September but slowed to 17,000 jobs, below the 12-month average pace of 33,000 per month. Hospitals added more than 12,000 jobs, which the piece reads as clinical staffing holding steady, and ambulatory care rose by 13,400. Long-term nursing and residential care lost 8,700 positions. Across the whole economy, employers added only 29,000 jobs in September, and the unemployment rate rose to 4.2 percent per the federal report. The article notes inflation and prices are higher while wages are not keeping up with worker needs. July and August employment gains were revised down by a combined 60,000 jobs. Long-term unemployment (27 weeks or more) was essentially unchanged at 1.9 million, representing 27.1 percent of all unemployed people, per the Bureau of Labor Statistics.

The piece then lists healthcare FM roles it says reflect the ambulatory care and hospital hiring trend: Safety Manager and Facilities Coordinator at UC Davis (Davis, CA); Manager, Facilities Management at Ochsner Health (New Orleans, LA); Senior Medical Planner at Leo A Daly (Washington, DC); Manager Facilities Operations at Nicklaus Children's Health System (Miami, FL); Facilities Supervisor at Oregon Health & Science University (Portland, OR); and Facilities Engineer at Leon Property Management (Doral, FL).

It closes with promotional framing for the FMLink Job Board, which connects facility managers, planners and commercial planning and design professionals across disciplines and career stages with employers, and says the Career Center offers thousands of FM job opportunities plus career planning advice for both professionals and employers. The item is essentially a recurring labor-market-plus-job-board roundup rather than analysis of workplace operations, technology or facilities practice.
